title: Vinorelbine IV · advanced breast cancer

agents.name: Vinorelbine
agents.mechanism: Disrupts the machinery of cell division
agents.explanation: Vinorelbine disrupts the tiny structures a cell needs to divide. This can stop cancer cells multiplying. Healthy blood-forming cells, gut cells and nerves can also be affected.
agents.watch: Use the treating unit’s 24-hour emergency number and local fever threshold. Contact immediately for fever/chills, sudden illness, breathlessness/chest pain, uncontrolled vomiting, severe abdominal pain/obstruction symptoms, bleeding or severe allergy. Do not wait until the next visit.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Nerve effects and uncommon lung/heart toxicity

purpose: Aim to slow or shrink advanced breast cancer and help symptoms while balancing side effects. Duration depends on benefit, tolerability and the agreed plan; a fixed number of cycles or a guaranteed survival improvement is not promised.
schedule_summary: 30 mg/m² onDays 1 and 8 every 21 days. Consultant may consider 25 mg/m² for poor marrow reserve; the dose is individualised after toxicity. Repeated 21-day cycles until progression/unacceptable toxicity; team review determines continuation.

support.title: Sickness plan
support.text: No routine preventive anti-sickness medicine is usually required for this IV regimen. Ask for a rescue plan and report uncontrolled symptoms.

support.title: Bowel care
support.text: Agree a constipation plan, particularly if using opioids or ondansetron. Severe abdominal pain, swelling, repeated vomiting or inability to pass stool/gas needs urgent assessment; do not simply add laxatives.

support.title: Medicines and vaccines
support.text: Check every new prescription, supplement and vaccine with the team; avoid grapefruit. Live vaccines and interacting medicines need review.

questions.q: Can IV and oral vinorelbine be exchanged?
questions.a: For IV use only; intrathecal administration may be fatal. Oral and IV vinorelbine are not interchangeablemg-for-mg. Stop infusion and tell staff immediately about pain, burning, swelling or leakage at the IV site; extravasation can damage tissue.
Repeated 21-day cycles until progression/unacceptable toxicity; team review determines continuation.

questions.q: Do I need regular heart scans?
questions.a: Review cardiovascular history and new symptoms. These monotherapy NCCP protocols do not mandate the serial LVEF/echo schedule used for anthracyclines or trastuzumab; arrange cardiac tests when clinically indicated.

questions.q: How long is an infusion visit?
questions.a: The source describes a short infusion followed by a saline flush. Your unit confirms the product-specific infusion instructions and complete visit length, including blood results, preparation and observation.

evidence.title: Why this treatment may be chosen
evidence.intro: Vinorelbine has shown activity in advanced breast cancer. Expected benefit depends on cancer biology, earlier treatment and health; historical trial averages do not predict an individual result.
evidence.interpretation: The team considers previous treatment, cancer features, health and your priorities. A response in a trial cannot guarantee benefit for an individual.
evidence.limitations: Evidence and alternatives are discussed for your exact setting. Trial survival averages are not an individual prediction.

items.title: How treatment is given
items.text: NCCP specifies 50 mL sodium chloride 0.9% over 15 minutes followed by 250 mL saline. Current Navelbine SmPC says 6–10 minutes: product/local-pharmacy reconciliation is required. Do not promise a total visit length; preparation, tests and observation add time.

details.title: Individual instructions
details.text: NCCP specifies 50 mL sodium chloride 0.9% over 15 minutes followed by 250 mL saline. Current Navelbine SmPC says 6–10 minutes: product/local-pharmacy reconciliation is required. Do not promise a total visit length; preparation, tests and observation add time.

anatomy: White blood cells can fall, raising the risk of infection. Anaemia can cause tiredness or breathlessness; low platelets can cause bruising or bleeding. Blood tests guide delays and dose changes. Fever, shaking chills or feeling suddenly unwell need the oncology emergency contact immediately.

The bowel can slow down and nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea or sore mouth can occur. Use the prescribed bowel and anti-sickness plan. Severe abdominal pain, swelling, repeated vomiting or inability to pass stool/gas needs urgent assessment for ileus; do not simply take extra laxatives.
Nerve effects may change sensation, grip, walking or bowel movement. Report changes early because the next dose may need to wait or be reduced.
Tiredness, hair thinning/loss and liver-test changes can occur. Pace activities and tell the team if eating, drinking or daily tasks become difficult.
New chest pain, sudden or worsening breathlessness, or severe allergic symptoms need urgent medical help. Previous heart disease and interacting medicines need review before treatment.
Tell staff immediately about burning, pain, swelling or leakage.
